gaps.sentence: She smiled ___ the waiter and ordered tea.
The project failed through a lack ___ funding.
He was charged ___ driving without insurance.
gaps.explanation: 'Charge somebody with an offence' — legal collocation.

gaps.sentence: I mistook him ___ one of the technicians — he was actually the new director.
gaps.explanation: 'Mistake somebody for somebody else' = wrongly believe they are that person.

gaps.sentence: Local traders have benefited enormously ___ the new footfall.
gaps.explanation: 'Benefit from' = gain an advantage from something.

gaps.sentence: Police suspect him ___ faking the documents.
She has a good relationship ___ her students.
gaps.explanation: a relationship WITH somebody (BETWEEN two parties).
